title: No Python CI workflow exists to catch test-config drift
body: The repository has no CI workflow that runs Python tests. `.github/workflows/go.yml` explicitly states "The Python tree has no workflow in this repo" and its `paths` filter excludes `tests/`. This allowed `tests/test_config.py` to assert `DEPTH_PROVER_CAPS[DepthProfile.QUICK] == 10` while `config.py` held `20` since commit `a6eaa79` (2026-03-12) without detection for ~5 months.
evidence: Step 1: Only CI workflow is `.github/workflows/go.yml`. Step 2: File comment at line 1 says "The Python tree has no workflow in this repo". Step 3: `paths` filter on push/PR includes only `go/**`, `docker-compose.go.yml`, `.github/workflows/go.yml`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `README.md`, `agentfield-package.yaml`, `src/cloudsecurity_af/app.py` — `tests/` is excluded. Step 4: `pyproject.toml` defines `testpaths = ["tests"]` but this is never invoked by CI. Step 5: The stale test asserting QUICK==10 persisted from March 2026 until this PR.

title: Go port explicitly documents that the Python test assertion is stale and fails on main
body: The Go port's `config.go` contains a reviewer note stating that `tests/test_config.py` asserts `DEPTH_PROVER_CAPS[QUICK] == 10` while `config.py` says `20`, and explicitly calls the Python test "STALE" and notes it "fails on main today." This confirms the mismatch was known to the Go developers but remained unfixed in the Python test suite due to the missing CI.
evidence: Step 1: `go/internal/config/config.go` lines 137-141 contain: "NOTE for reviewers: tests/test_config.py on main asserts DEPTH_PROVER_CAPS[QUICK] == 10, but config.py says 20 — that Python test is STALE and fails on main today (verified with this repo's interpreter)." Step 2: `go/internal/config/config_test.go` lines 406-411 repeat: "The Python test asserts DEPTH_PROVER_CAPS[QUICK] == 10, but config.py has declared 20 since the value was raised; that Python assertion FAILS on main today." Step 3: The Go code follows the config value (20), not the stale test.

title: Stale prover-cap test masked config drift for months on a security-boundary control
dimension_name: Confirm QUICK=20 and STANDARD=30 are intentional security-boundary caps
body: The `test_prover_caps` test asserted `DEPTH_PROVER_CAPS[QUICK] == 10` while `config.py` held `20` since the bulk rename commit (7307507). The Go port explicitly verified this test fails on main and called it stale. If CI executed pytest on this file, it would fail continuously from the rename onward. The PR corrects the assertion but does not investigate why the mismatch persisted undetected or whether CI was actually running this test path. For a security-boundary control that limits proof-chain depth, an extended test/config drift without detection is a reliability gap.
evidence: Step 1: Initial CloudProve-AF commit 86cae2f set `DEPTH_PROVER_CAPS[QUICK] = 10` with matching test assertion. Step 2: Rename commit 7307507 created `src/cloudsecurity_af/config.py` with `QUICK = 20` but did not update `tests/test_config.py`, leaving the test asserting `== 10`. Step 3: Go port `go/internal/config/config.go` lines 137-141 notes: "that Python test is STALE and fails on main today (verified with this repo's interpreter)." Step 4: Go test `config_test.go` lines 404-416 is named `TestDepthProverCaps_QuickIsTwentyNotTheStalePythonTestValue` with comment "WITH A DELIBERATE CORRECTION" confirming the Python assertion fails. Step 5: The PR fixes the Python test but does not address why CI did not catch this failure or whether the test path was skipped.
